author: C

components.title: Part A: monthly balance simulation
components.what: Apply each month's transaction, then fee if below $1500, then 0.5% interest, sequentially for 15 months to get final balance.

components.title: Part B: overtime pay calculation
components.what: Compute daily pay using 1x/1.5x/2x tiers for each of 14 days and sum for total gross pay.

components.title: Part C: inclusion-exclusion divisibility count
components.what: Count integers 1-12000 divisible by 4, 6, or 9 via inclusion-exclusion, then subtract those also divisible by 17.

components.title: Part D: big product digit sum
components.what: Multiply the four numbers together and sum the decimal digits of the resulting product.

log.author: A
log.draft:
FINAL ANSWER:

Part A: Simulated month-by-month with transaction, then fee if balance<$1,500, then 0.5% interest. No month triggered the fee (balance always ≥1500). Sequential computation gives final balance ≈ $4473.44.

Part B: Daily overtime converted to equivalent regular-rate hours (1x up to 8, 1.5x for 8–12, 2x beyond 12). Total equivalent hours = 147.0. Gross pay = 147.0 × $31.20 = $4,586.40. Verified via day-by-day breakdown (e.g., 12.5h day → 8+4(1.5)+0.5(2)=15 eq. hours).

Part C: Inclusion-exclusion for divisibility by 4, 6, or 9 (lcm(4,6)=12, lcm(4,9)=36, lcm(6,9)=18, lcm(4,6,9)=36):
Union = 3000+2000+1333−1000−333−666+333 = 4667.
Subtract those also divisible by 17 via inclusion-exclusion on lcm(4,17)=68, lcm(6,17)=102, lcm(9,17)=153, lcm(12,17)=204, lcm(36,17)=612, lcm(18,17)=306:
176+117+78−58−19−39+19 = 274.
Final count = 4667−274 = 4393.

Part D: 81494×3591=292,644,954; ×593=173,538,457,722; ×8661=1,503,016,582,330,242.
Digit sum = 1+5+0+3+0+1+6+5+8+2+3+3+0+2+4+2 = 45.

FINAL: 4473.44; 4586.40; 4393; 45

Untested arithmetic; the stated final balance is not supported by the shown working, and fee/interest order can change the result.
Missing day-by-day calculation for all 14 days; the total equivalent hours may be wrong.
Wrong figure likely; the inclusion-exclusion for divisibility by 4, 6, or 9 and subtraction of multiples of 17 may double-count or mis-handle lcm terms.
